question.text: Two long straight wires <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> carrying equal current <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> each were kept parallel to each other at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> distance. Magnitude of magnetic force experienced by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> length of wire <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>F</mi><mn mathvariant="italic">1</mn></msub></math>. If distance between wires is halved and currents on them are doubled, force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> length of wire <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> will be:

solution.text:
As we know, force per unit length between two parallel straight wires is given by,  F=μ0i1i22πd.

Therefore, required ratio

F1 F2=μ0(10)22π(5×10-2)μ0(20)22π52×10-2=18

⇒F2=8F1
